[P1] 北京市绿色印刷工程
优秀少儿读物绿色印刷示范项目
儿童情绪管理与性格培养绘本
第四辑 成长进行时
不要告状，
陈非是大事！
一个告状的故事
[美]珍妮·弗朗兹·兰塞姆(Jeanie Franz Ransom) 著
[美]杰基·厄本诺维克(Jackie Urbanovi) 绘 苏海泉 译
美国心理学会
官方授权
APA
化学工业出版社

[P2] 儿童情绪管理与性格培养绘本
第四辑 成长进行时
不要告状，除非是大事！
一个告状的故事
Don't Squeal Unless It's a Big Deal
A Tale of Tattletales
[美] 珍妮·弗朗兹·兰塞姆（Jeanie Franz Ransom）著
[美] 杰基·厄本诺维克（Jackie Urbanovic）绘
苏海泉 译
化学工业出版社
·北京·

[P3] 麦克尼尔太太（以下简称麦太太）的班里
有19名学生，19个爱告状的小家伙。

[P4] 当杰西卡一路小跑来到麦太太桌前，一场好戏就此开始。
“皮特揪我的辫子！”
“那一定很疼，”麦太太说，“你告诉皮特你有多疼了吗？”
杰西卡点了点头。
麦太太说：“让我们听听皮特怎么说。”

[P5] 皮特慢吞吞地走到麦太太桌前。
“杰西卡说你揪她的辫子。”麦太太说。
“我没揪！”皮特说。
“你揪了！”杰西卡说。

[P6] “你们都有权讲出自己的感受，”麦太太说，“也都有权在学校感到安全和开心。不过，开心的前提，是遵守‘管好自己的手’这条规定。”
麦太太接着说：“既然杰西卡的辫子还好好的，皮特看起来也不是那么危险，那么现在你们都回到自己的座位吧。”
杰西卡跺着脚离开了。
皮特气呼呼地离开了。
麦太太哼起了《山谷里的农夫》。

[P7] 麦太太举起杯子，刚想喝一口，斯蒂文小跑着过来了。
“瑞秋把我的粉色笔拿走了，我向她要了两次，她都没还！”
麦太太放下杯子。
“斯蒂文，很高兴你能先跟瑞秋沟通，试着自己解决问题，”麦太太说，“也许今天瑞秋的听力不大好，我们一起去看看究竟是怎么回事。”

[P8] “斯蒂文找不到他的粉色笔了，”麦太太问瑞秋，“你看到了吗？”“我已经还给他了！”瑞秋大叫道，“现在是我的找不到了！”“那是因为你用光了！”皮特说，“你一直在用它画小猪啊！”瑞秋抱怨道：“你们知道的，这些都是我的自画像！我能怎么办？难道把自己涂成绿色？”“你知道我们班级的规定，瑞秋，”麦太太说，“如果你想借东西，先问问别人。这是对待朋友的正确方法——这样才能友谊长存。”

[P9] 麦太太端起杯子，刚喝了一口，梅根又来报告：
“弗兰克叫苏克胖母猪。”
麦太太不得不匆匆咽下去，她清了清喉咙，希望自己牙齿上没粘上玉米粒。“我很高兴你非常清楚班级的规定，”麦太太说，“你是对的！我们不能给别人起绰号。”

[P10] “还有，我们不插手自己不该管的事。”麦太太说。
“我知道你很想帮忙，但是，如果这是弗兰克和苏克之间的事，那么他们就要自己解决；如果他们解决不了，那就是我的事，作为老师，要帮他们解决。而你要做的，”麦太太补充说，“就是照顾好你自己，对你来说，这是最重要的！"
梅根蹦蹦跳跳地回到了自己的座位。但这时……

[P11] 混战开始了！
“乔纳森把我的纸撕破了！”
“罗比朝我吹气！”
“劳拉盯着我看！”
“艾米丽说我的课桌是猪槽！”
“杰瑞米总是哼出声，我都没法专心学习了！”
“山姆在挖鼻孔！”

[P12] 大家不停地挤到麦太太的桌子前——她的耐心慢慢耗尽了——她站了起来。学生们立刻都坐回了座位。
麦太太说：“在吃午饭前，我想我们需要增加一条新班规。”“一条非常重要的班规。”她补充说，“谁能告诉我，什么是告状？”大家七嘴八舌说起来。
麦太太摇摇铃，让大家安静下来，然后继续讲。“告状，”麦太太说，“就是专指打小报告。我知道你们都明白它是什么意思。”

[P13] 新班规：
不要告状，
除非是大事！

“我很高兴你这么问，”麦太太说，
“告状就是说，当有人做了你不喜欢的事或讲了你不喜欢的话，你去告诉大人——而不是先告诉他本人。”

“大多数小朋友之间发生的事，是可以自己解决的。”麦太太说，“通常通过交谈、倾听和互相帮助就可以解决。”

有人低头看地板。有人互相瞅（chǒu）瞅。
有人眼盯着天花板，好像突然在那发现了感兴趣的东西。麦太太开始在黑板上写字。“这是我们的新班规！”麦太太说。“这是什么意思？”杰西卡问。

[P14] “但是有时，”麦太太说，
“会发生一些比较大的事，比如有人受伤或处境危险，

或者伤害小动物，

有人伤害你，

或者破坏一些属于大家的公共设施。”

[P15] 新班规：
不要告状，
除非是大事！

“这时候就可以来告状——因为这是大事！大事就是紧急的事，这时候你需要找大人帮忙！”
奥斯卡举手说：“我知道这不是什么大事。麦太太，但是我太饿了，都能吃下一大草垛了！”
麦太太笑着说：“我也是！等我们回来以后，再来练习刚才学的东西。”

[P16] 但是那天下午，麦太太刚要关教室的门，凯蒂又跑来告状：“课间休息时，珍妮一直占着秋千。”
麦太太指着黑板说：“还记得我们刚学了什么吗？”凯蒂点点头。
“既然你知道我们的规定，那么你应该直接告诉珍妮。”

[P17] “告诉我什么？”珍妮在教室的另一边嚷嚷。
“你一直占着秋千！”凯蒂也叫喊起来。
“你又没说你想玩！”珍妮说。
“一直没轮到我！”凯蒂说。
“不是我的错，”皮特说，“这次不是我的错！”
“是卡洛琳的错！”苏克说。
“谁是卡洛琳？”奥斯卡问。
“她根本就不在我们班！”弗兰克说。

[P18] 砰！麦太太不见了。“您没事吧？”梅根问。
麦太太没有回答。她的眼睛闭着，尾巴也无力地耷拉着，有一只耳朵还有点红。
“快！给医务室打电话！告诉他们，这里有紧急情况！”“快去找护士！”“快去通知隔壁的哈姆林太太！”

[P19] 这天下午晚些时候，大家去医务室看望麦太太。
“我们很抱歉今天告了这么多状。”杰西卡说。
“我们不是存心想气您的。”皮特说。

[P20] “这都是我们的错！”凯蒂哭了起来。
“谁都没错，”麦太太说，“这是个意外，我踩到溅出来的汤，滑倒了。当时一定很乱吧。”
“我们以为您被气炸了！”杰瑞米说。
“简直乱极了。”奥斯卡补充道。
“您最好别再吃那些东西了。”瑞秋说，“您需要好好照顾自己！”

[P21] “看来你们都能很好地解决问题了！”麦太太说，“我受伤时你们所说的话，说明你们是知道应该怎么做做的！”
“这是因为您是好老师。”杰西卡说。“你们也是好学生。”麦太太说。
“我们还需要多练习。”凯蒂说。
“学新东西的时候一向如此，”麦太太说，“我们开始练习吧！”
“不要告状，除非是大事！”

[P2] Children's Emotional Management and Character Development Picture Book
Series 4: Growing Up
Don't Tattle Unless It's a Big Deal!
A Story About Tattling
Don't Squeal Unless It's a Big Deal
A Tale of Tattletales
[USA] Jeanie Franz Ransom (author)
[USA] Jackie Urbanovic (illustrator)
Translated by Su Haiquan
Chemical Industry Press
·Beijing·

[P3] Mrs. MacNeill (hereafter referred to as Mrs. Mac) has 19 students in her class, 19 little kids who love to tattle.

[P4] When Jessica ran up to Mrs. Mc's desk, a good show began.
"Pete pulled my braid!"
"That must have hurt," Mrs. Mc said, "Did you tell Pete how much it hurt?"
Jessica nodded.
Mrs. Mc said, "Let's hear what Pete has to say."

[P5] Pete slowly walked to Mrs. Mc's desk.
"Jessica says you pulled her braid," Mrs. Mc said.
"I didn't!" Pete said.
"You did!" Jessica said.

[P6] "You all have the right to share your feelings," Mrs. McTee said, "and you all have the right to feel safe and happy at school. But the前提 for being happy is following the rule 'Keep your hands to yourself.'"
Mrs. McTee continued, "Since Jessica's braid is still fine and Pete doesn't look so dangerous, now you both go back to your seats."
Jessica stomped off.
Pete left, fuming.
Mrs. McTee hummed "The Farmer in the Dell."

[P7] Mrs. McTee raised her cup, just about to take a sip, when Steven ran over.
"Rachel took my pink pen, I asked her twice, and she hasn't given it back!"
Mrs. McTee put down her cup.
"Steven, I'm glad you tried to communicate with Rachel first and attempted to solve the problem yourself," Mrs. McTee said, "Maybe Rachel's hearing isn't great today. Let's go check what's really going on."

[P8] "Steven can't find his pink pen," Mrs. McTee asked Rachel, "did you see it?" "I already gave it back to him!" Rachel shouted, "Now mine is missing!" "That's because you used it all up!" Pete said, "You've been drawing little pigs with it!" Rachel complained, "You know, these are all my self-portraits! What am I supposed to do? Paint myself green?" "You know our class rule, Rachel," Mrs. McTee said, "If you want to borrow something, ask the other person first. That's the right way to treat friends—this is how friendships last."

[P9] Mrs. McTavish picked up her cup, took a sip, and then Megan reported: 
"Frank called Sue Piggy Fat Pig." 
Mrs. McTavish had to swallow quickly. She cleared her throat, hoping no corn kernels were stuck in her teeth. "I'm glad you're very clear about the class rules," Mrs. McTavish said, "You're right! We can't give others nicknames."

[P10] "Besides, we don't interfere in things that aren't our business," said Mrs. McTavish.
"I know you want to help, but if this is between Frank and Sukie, then they need to solve it themselves; if they can't, then it's my job as a teacher to help them. And what you need to do," Mrs. McTavish added, "is take care of yourself. That's the most important thing for you!"
Megan skipped back to her own seat. But then...

[P11] The chaos has begun!
"Jonathan tore my paper!"
"Robbie is blowing air at me!"
"Laura is staring at me!"
"Emily said my desk is a pig trough!"
"Jeremy is always humming, I can't focus on my work!"
"Sam is picking his nose!"

[P12] The students kept crowding up to Mrs. McTavish's desk—her patience was running out—so she stood up. The students immediately sat back down.
Mrs. McTavish said, "Before lunch, I think we need to add a new classroom rule." "A very important rule," she added. "Who can tell me what 'tattling' means?" The class started talking all at once.
Mrs. McTavish rang the bell to quiet everyone down, then continued. "'Tattling,'" Mrs. McTavish said, "means specifically telling on someone. I know you all understand what that means."

[P13] New Class Rule:
Don't tattle,
unless it's a big deal!

"I'm glad you asked," Mrs. McTatt said,
"Tattling means that when someone does something you don't like or says something you don't like, you go tell an adult — not first tell the person themselves."

"Most things that happen between kids can be solved by themselves," Mrs. McTatt said, "Usually through talking, listening, and helping each other."

Some looked down at the floor. Some looked at each other (chǒu) curiously.
Some stared at the ceiling, as if they'd suddenly discovered something interesting. Mrs. McTatt began writing on the blackboard. "This is our new class rule!" Mrs. McTatt said. "What does it mean?" Jessica asked.

[P14] "But sometimes," Mrs. McTavish said, 
"there are bigger things, like if someone is hurt or in danger, 

or if someone is hurting small animals, 

or if someone is hurting you, 

or if someone is breaking things that belong to everyone, like public facilities."

[P15] New Class Rule:
Don't tattle,
unless it's a big deal!

"This is when you can come and tell — because it's a big deal! A big deal is an emergency, and that's when you need to ask an adult for help!"
Oscar raised his hand and said, "I know this isn't a big deal, Mrs. McTavish. But I'm so hungry, I could eat a whole bale of hay!"
Mrs. McTavish smiled and said, "Me too! After we come back, we'll practice what we just learned."

[P16] But that afternoon, as Mrs. McTavish was about to close the classroom door, Katie ran up to tattle: "During recess, Jenny kept taking the swing." 
Mrs. McTavish pointed to the board and said, "Do you remember what we just learned?" Katie nodded. 
"Since you know our rule, you should tell Jenny directly."

[P17] "Tell me what?" Jenny shouted from the other side of the classroom.
"You've been taking up the swing!" Katie shouted back.
"You didn't say you wanted to play!" Jenny said.
"I haven't gotten a turn yet!" Katie said.
"It's not my fault," Pete said, "This time it's not my fault!"
"It's Caroline's fault!" Suk said.
"Who is Caroline?" Oscar asked.
"She's not even in our class!" Frank said.

[P18] Bang! Mrs. McTavish is gone. "Are you okay?" Megan asked.
Mrs. McTavish didn't answer. Her eyes were closed, her tail drooped limply, and one ear was a little red.
"Quick! Call the nurse's office! Tell them there's an emergency here!" "Go find a nurse!" "Quick, tell Mrs. Hamlin next door!"

[P19] Later that afternoon, everyone went to the nurse's office to visit Mrs. McTavish.
"We're sorry we tattled so much today," said Jessica.
"We didn't mean to make you mad," said Pete.

[P20] "This is all our fault!" Katie cried.
"Nobody's at fault," Mrs. McTavish said, "It was an accident. I stepped on spilled soup and slipped. It must have been very chaotic then."
"We thought you got blown up from anger!" Jeremy said.
"It was absolutely chaotic," Oscar added.
"You'd better not eat those things anymore," Rachel said, "You need to take good care of yourself!"

[P21] "It looks like you're all doing a great job solving problems!" Mrs. McTavish said. "The things you said when I was hurt show that you know what to do!"
"That's because you're a great teacher," Jessica said. "You're great students too," Mrs. McTavish said.
"We still need more practice," Katie said.
"That's how it always is when learning something new," Mrs. McTavish said, "Let's start practicing!"
"Don't tattle, unless it's a big deal!"
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本封面，标题为《不要告状，陈非是大事！》，讲述一个关于告状的故事，由美国作者珍妮·弗朗兹·兰塞姆创作，插图由杰基·厄本诺维克绘制，苏海泉翻译。画面中两只小猪在教室里，一只指向另一只，后者正在大哭，地上散落着纸张和书本。
[P2] 本页为绘本的扉页，展示了书名《不要告状，除非是大事！》、副标题、作者、插画师、译者及出版社信息，并配有一只小猪的圆形插图。
[P3] 画面展示了一个充满混乱的教室，许多小动物学生在争吵、哭泣或告状，文字说明麦太太的班里有19名爱告状的学生。
[P4] 杰西卡向麦太太告状，说皮特揪了她的辫子，麦太太询问她是否告诉了皮特有多疼，并决定听听皮特的说法。
[P5] 皮特被杰西卡告状揪她的辫子，麦太太询问后，皮特否认，杰西卡坚持说他揪了，双方各执一词。
[P6] 麦太太在处理杰西卡和皮特的争执后，要求他们回到座位，并强调了‘管好自己的手’的规则，随后她哼起了歌。
[P7] 斯蒂文向麦太太告状，说瑞秋拿走了他的粉色笔且未归还。麦太太鼓励他先与瑞秋沟通，并提议一起去查看情况，以帮助他学会自己解决问题。
[P8] 麦太太处理斯蒂文和瑞秋关于粉色笔的争执，瑞秋声称已归还，但斯蒂文找不到，皮特指出瑞秋用笔画小猪，麦太太借此机会教导学生借物需先询问，以维护友谊。
[P9] 梅根向麦太太告状，说弗兰克给苏克起了绰号“胖母猪”，麦太太肯定了梅根遵守班级规定的行为，并重申不能给别人起绰号的规则。
[P10] 麦太太教导梅根不要插手他人之间的矛盾，强调学生应先自己解决问题，老师只在必要时介入，并提醒梅根照顾好自己。梅根回到座位后，故事引出新的情节。
[P11] 教室里爆发了混乱，学生们纷纷向老师告状，抱怨彼此的不当行为，如撕纸、吹气、盯着看、挖鼻孔等，场面一片嘈杂。
[P12] 麦太太因学生不断告状而感到疲惫，她宣布要增加一条新班规，并向学生们解释“告状”就是打小报告，引导他们理解这一概念。
[P13] 麦太太在黑板上写下新班规“不要告状，除非是大事！”，并向学生们解释告状的含义，强调小朋友之间的问题应先自己解决。学生们对此感到困惑和好奇，杰西卡提问新规则的意思。
[P14] 麦太太向学生们解释，在什么情况下可以告状，例如有人受伤、处境危险、伤害小动物或破坏公共设施。
[P15] 麦太太在黑板上写下新班规“不要告状，除非是大事！”，并解释了“大事”的含义。学生奥斯卡举手表示自己太饿，麦太太笑着回应，提议等回来后再练习新学的内容。
[P16] 凯蒂向麦太太告状说珍妮占着秋千，麦太太提醒她应直接与珍妮沟通，而不是告状。
[P17] 凯蒂和珍妮因秋千使用问题发生争执，其他同学也纷纷加入争论，互相指责，场面混乱，老师在旁观察。
[P18] 麦太太突然消失，学生们发现她倒下后非常惊慌，纷纷喊叫着要通知医务室、护士和隔壁的哈姆林太太，场面一片混乱。
[P19] 学生们在下午晚些时候来到医务室看望麦太太，杰西卡和皮特向她道歉，表示他们并非有意惹她生气。
[P20] 学生们在医务室看望麦太太，凯蒂哭着道歉，麦太太解释自己是因意外滑倒，并安慰孩子们，其他学生也表达了担忧和关心。
[P21] 麦太太表扬学生们在她受伤后表现出了良好的问题解决能力，学生们也表达了对老师的喜爱和感激。麦太太鼓励大家继续练习新学的班规，并重申了“不要告状，除非是大事”的规则。
